theory.intro: Two triangles are similar when one is an enlargement of the other — the same shape, with every side scaled by the same factor. Four minimum tests decide similarity, and the reasoning is written out in full every time.
facts: **Equiangular (AAA)**: at least two pairs of equal corresponding angles — the third pair must then be equal by the angle sum.
**SSS**: three pairs of corresponding sides in the same ratio.
**SAS**: two pairs of corresponding sides in the same ratio and the included angle equal.
**RHS**: both triangles right-angled, with the hypotenuses and another pair of corresponding sides in the same ratio.
The scale factor is $\frac{\text{image}}{\text{original}}$ — divide a side of the second triangle by its corresponding side in the first.
steps: Pair up corresponding parts: shortest side with shortest side, largest angle with largest angle.
For the side tests, divide each side of one triangle by its corresponding side in the other and compare the ratios.
Match the pattern to a test — equiangular (AAA), SSS, SAS or RHS — or conclude the triangles are not similar.

mastery.solution_text:
Left triangle: the base angles are equal, so each is $\frac{180^{\circ}-130^{\circ}}{2}=25^{\circ}$.
Right triangle: both base angles are $25^{\circ}$, so the apex angle is $180^{\circ}-25^{\circ}-25^{\circ}=130^{\circ}$.
Both triangles have angles $25^{\circ}$, $25^{\circ}$ and $130^{\circ}$.
There are at least two pairs of equal corresponding angles, so the triangles are similar (equiangular, AAA).

Match sides in size order: shortest $\frac{8}{6}=1.33\ldots$, middle $\frac{12}{9}=1.33\ldots$, longest $\frac{18}{12}=1.5$.
The third pair of corresponding sides is not in the same ratio as the other two.
The SSS similarity test fails, so the triangles are not similar — the two sides labelled $12$ are not corresponding sides.

The hypotenuse is the side opposite the right angle: $13$ in the first triangle and $19.5$ in the second.
$\frac{19.5}{13}=1.5$
$\frac{7.5}{5}=1.5$
The hypotenuses and another pair of corresponding sides are in the same ratio, so the triangles are similar (RHS).
